title: Independence is an outcome, not a single spending number
scope: Sintered NdFeB and Nd/Pr/Dy/Tb, including purchased iron/ferroboron dependencies; research only.
status: Bounded public evidence and decision framework; not an optimized national investment plan.

definitions.meaning: Serve specified U.S. customer-qualified demand without China-origin feed, processing, metals/alloys/magnets or critical China-controlled process inputs, using an explicitly selected set of trusted countries.
definitions.boundary: Foreign steps count only after process/feed origin, access and readiness are verified. Supplier ownership does not establish source origin.
unresolved: Eligibility of existing China-origin stocks and recycled scrap
Equipment, spares, technology and minor-input origin rules
definitions.label: China-independent with allies
definitions.short: U.S. and explicitly approved allied routes; every relevant origin and access condition must be verified.

definitions.meaning: Serve specified qualified demand with U.S.-located mining or approved domestic secondary feed, separation, metal/master-alloy conversion, magnet production and finishing/qualification.
definitions.boundary: Allied feed or foreign conversion fails this strict geographic definition. U.S. ownership of foreign assets does not establish U.S. production.
unresolved: Eligibility of domestic recovered China-origin magnets
Reagents, equipment, spares and minor additives
Whether embedded finished goods and motor assembly must also be onshored
definitions.label: Entirely U.S.-located chain
definitions.short: All required steps and eligible feed meet a strict U.S. geographic boundary.

national_total.finding: No verified public primary national capex estimate found that specifies demand, horizon and one of the independence definitions.
national_total.limitation: A bounded search finding, not proof that no estimate exists. Public sources provide a global model, partial project estimates, financing packages and redacted survey costs.

options.upfront: Initial purchase and working capital; an asset, not construction capex.
options.recurring: Finance, storage, logistics, rotation/quality losses, net of release proceeds.
options.readiness: Early short disruption only if approved parts can be acquired and released.
options.allied_definition: Domestic or verified China-independent ally parts; decide eligibility of old China-origin stocks.
options.domestic_definition: Only eligible U.S. production/feed; stock does not create domestic capacity.
options.priority_condition: An immediate short service gap and usable purchasable stock.
options.card_description: Bridge a short service gap, if usable parts can be acquired.

options.readiness: Existing production can be earlier than new construction; a new customer or grade can still need approval.
options.allied_definition: Eligible after feed/process origin, access and allocation verification.
options.domestic_definition: Foreign steps can bridge service but fail strict geographic independence.
options.priority_condition: An eligible complete route can meet required grades and dates.
options.card_description: Check a complete eligible route, not just a supplier address.

options.upfront: Incremental construction, testing, tooling and training.
options.recurring: Added feed, utilities, labor, reagents, maintenance and yield loss.
options.readiness: Project-specific; establish the bottleneck of the complete route.
options.allied_definition: Expand a U.S. or eligible allied node.
options.domestic_definition: Expand U.S. nodes with eligible domestic feed.
options.priority_condition: The increment unlocks qualified service because other stages are ready.
options.card_description: Expand the stage that actually unlocks accepted supply.

options.upfront: Remaining plant/infrastructure capital, commissioning, qualification and working capital.
options.recurring: Full plant operating costs and sustaining investment.
options.readiness: Examples target commissioning from 2028; White Mesa Phase2 mid-2029 is conditional. These are not accepted-delivery dates.
options.allied_definition: Build a complete route using eligible diversified feed/conversion.
options.domestic_definition: Every required step and feed must satisfy the U.S. boundary.
options.priority_condition: A persistent gap after readiness, with credible feed, technology and customer demand.
options.card_description: Cost a complete future route through commissioning and acceptance.

options.recurring: Mining, reagents, waste, transport and co-product economics.
options.readiness: IEA newly announced ex-China projects average around eight years; not a universal U.S. project date.
options.allied_definition: A broader resource/project set can qualify.
options.domestic_definition: Domestic assays, deposits and permits restrict choices.
options.priority_condition: A long-lived compatible feed or element-mix gap binds a complete path.
options.card_description: Resolve a long-lived compatible feed or element-mix gap.

options.upfront: Collection/segregation/recycling capital or redesign and requalification.
options.readiness: Potentially earlier for proven prompt scrap or accepted designs; later for new collection/technology.
options.allied_definition: Cross-border secondary feed/conversion depends on origin rules.
options.domestic_definition: Domestic secondary-feed eligibility must be defined.
options.priority_condition: Verified yield or performance benefit within the service horizon.
constraints: Recovered feed versus qualified finished product
options.card_description: Reduce primary exposure only with verified yield and performance.

cost_ledgers.label: Upfront cash & assets
cost_ledgers.detail: Remaining incremental construction, one-off engineering/qualification, initial incremental inventory purchases and working capital.
cost_ledgers.rule: Keep sunk spending and acquisitions distinct. Stock purchase is an asset, not factory construction cost.

cost_ledgers.label: Recurring operations
cost_ledgers.detail: Plant operating and sustaining costs, inventory finance/storage/logistics, losses and rotation.
cost_ledgers.rule: State annual timing, release/sales proceeds and co-product economics separately. A yearly cost is not a one-off capex total.

cost_ledgers.label: Public fiscal cash & exposure
cost_ledgers.detail: Grants and tax credits; loan/equity cash and recoveries; guarantees; price-floor and offtake cash flows.
cost_ledgers.rule: Financing is not a second construction cost. Loan principal is not a free grant or an automatic reduction in resource cost.

framework.objective: Minimize unmet customer-qualified part demand over a specified disruption/recovery horizon, under upfront capital and readiness constraints.
framework.equation: min sum(t,g,scenario) probability[scenario] * criticality_weight[g] * unmet[g,t,scenario]; choose probability or worst-case aggregation explicitly.
framework.budget: Remaining incremental construction + one-off engineering/qualification + initial incremental stock purchase + working capital <= B. Set annual operating cash constraints separately.
framework.network: Use concentrate/oxide/metal/master-alloy/alloy/magnet/qualified-part nodes with actual assays, conversions and yields. Readiness, ramp, utilization, rejection, customer acceptance and available allocation constrain flows.
framework.path_check: Convert stage capacities to the same finished-part basis and take the bottleneck; do not add successive masses. Mass-balance recycled and internal scrap only once.
framework.demand: Separate U.S. assembly demand from imported embedded finished-goods demand. Add assembly-onshoring investment only if the chosen boundary requires it.
framework.project_costs: Record distinct incremental projects with scope, geography, price year, estimate class, contingency and remaining cash. Keep multi-stage campuses whole unless an engineering breakdown is public. Separate sunk spending and acquisitions.
framework.public_fiscal_costs: Maintain a separate ledger for grant/tax-credit cost, loan/equity cash and recoveries, guarantee exposure and price-floor/offtake cash flows. Financing does not add construction cost.
framework.inventory: Initial purchase = quantity * delivered qualified quote by form/grade. Annual carrying cost = finance + storage + logistics/insurance + losses/rotation discounts. Keep inventory assets and release proceeds separate. Only accessible conversion/acceptance makes upstream stocks usable.
framework.readiness: Use the critical path for the complete chain and customer acceptance. Do not equate commissioning with qualified delivery or add parallel work durations arbitrarily.
outputs: Budget versus qualified-service frontier with uncertainty
Bottleneck and earliest feasible date by part family
Remaining incremental capex and initial inventory cash separately
Annual carrying/operating costs and public fiscal exposure separately
Unmet customer-qualified demand under both definitions

Qualified inventory, quotes and storage terms
Supplier allocation, qualification and ramp dates
Assays, conversions, yields, scrap recovery and HREE process needs
Origin/access verification and correlated disruption scenarios
Operating costs, co-product revenues and finance terms

empirical_study.scope: One end-user and a small set of approved sintered NdFeB industrial-motor part families, with a U.S. assembly boundary. This is a proposed empirical study, not a national allocation.
next_inputs: Monthly orders and BOMs with grade/shape/acceptance
Accessible inventory, actual yields/ramp and supplier allocation
Incremental complete-path engineering and qualification quotes
empirical_study.design: Choose the planning horizon with the user. Test 3/6/12-month disruptions as explicitly illustrative sensitivity cases under both definitions. Optimize after missing inputs arrive; until then show bounds and unknowns.
empirical_study.deliverable: Reproducible route-level mass balance and qualified-service frontier; validate against accepted shipments.
empirical_study.scale_rule: Expand across more part families before making a national model. Do not multiply one campus cost by unverified national tonnage.

demand_example.scope: Selected applications; sintered plus bonded; direct plus embedded finished-goods demand
demand_example.locator: DOE Table10 printedp32/PDFp45; BIS Table2 p31
demand_example.scenario_basis: Aggressive decarbonization assumptions published in 2022; not observed 2026 demand.
limitations: Embedded imported goods do not necessarily create U.S. magnet-factory demand
Assumes 30GW U.S. offshore wind in 2030 and a 90% EV permanent-magnet share; update deployment, policy and technology assumptions
Do not add magnet mass to contained rare-earth demand

global_context: IEA’s approximately $60B requirement is global diversification outside China through 2035, not a U.S. budget. Announced project budgets cannot be summed into a national independence requirement.
